smol-01-c2.text: H. Peter Lu, Luying Xun, X. Sunney Xie (1998). Single-Molecule Enzymatic Dynamics. Science 282(5395), 1877-1882.
smol-01-c2.quote: There exists a memory effect: an enzymatic turnover is not independent of its previous turnovers.
smol-01-c2.claim: Catalytic turnover times within one molecule's trajectory are correlated: a slow turnover is followed by another slow turnover, which suggests the conformation persists.

smol-01-c1.text: Lu HP, Xun L, Xie XS (1998). Single-molecule enzymatic dynamics. Science (New York, N.Y.).
smol-01-c1.quote: A molecular memory phenomenon, in which an enzymatic turnover was not independent of its previous turnovers because of a slow fluctuation of protein conformation, was evidenced by spontaneous spectral fluctuation of FAD.
smol-01-c1.claim: In 1998, Lu, Xun, and Xie's single-molecule study of cholesterol oxidase revealed memory effects in catalytic turnover that were invisible in bulk steady-state kinetics

smol-04-c3.text: Liphardt J, Dumont S, Smith SB, Tinoco I, Bustamante C (2002). Equilibrium information from nonequilibrium measurements in an experimental test of Jarzynski's equality. Science (New York, N.Y.).
smol-04-c3.quote: In 1997, Jarzynski proved an equality relating the irreversible work to the equilibrium free energy difference, DeltaG.
smol-04-c3.claim: The 1997 Jarzynski equality looks impossible at first sight: an exact relation between equilibrium free-energy difference and the work done in arbitrarily fast, irreversible processes.

smol-05-c2.text: Betzig E, Patterson GH, Sougrat R, Lindwasser OW, Olenych S, Bonifacino JS, Davidson MW, Lippincott-Schwartz J, Hess HF (2006). Imaging intracellular fluorescent proteins at nanometer resolution. Science (New York, N.Y.).
smol-05-c2.quote: Numerous sparse subsets of photoactivatable fluorescent protein molecules were activated, localized (to approximately 2 to 25 nanometers), and then bleached.
smol-05-c2.claim: PALM (Photo-Activated Localisation Microscopy) from Eric Betzig and Harald Hess (2006, HHMI Janelia) uses photoactivatable fluorescent proteins (PA-GFP, mEos2, Dronpa)

smol-05-c3.text: Balzarotti F, Eilers Y, Gwosch KC, Gynnå AH, Westphal V, Stefani FD, Elf J, Hell SW (2017). Nanometer resolution imaging and tracking of fluorescent molecules with minimal photon fluxes. Science (New York, N.Y.).
smol-05-c3.quote: By probing the emitter with a local intensity minimum of excitation light, MINFLUX minimizes the fluorescence photons needed for high localization precision.
smol-05-c3.claim: Instead of imaging an emitter through a Gaussian PSF, MINFLUX excites it with a doughnut beam that has zero intensity at its centre.

smol-06-c2.text: Kasianowicz JJ, Brandin E, Branton D, Deamer DW (1996). Characterization of individual polynucleotide molecules using a membrane channel. Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences.
smol-06-c2.quote: We show that an electric field can drive single-stranded RNA and DNA molecules through a 2.6-nm diameter ion channel in a lipid bilayer membrane.
smol-06-c2.claim: The original Kasianowicz-Branton-Deamer 1996 demonstration showed that ssDNA could even be threaded through α-hemolysin.

smol-02-c2.text: Lukinavičius G, Umezawa K, Olivier N, Honigmann A, Yang G, Plass T, Mueller V, Reymond L, Corrêa IR, Luo ZG, Schultz C, Lemke EA, Heppenstall P, Eggeling C, Manley S, Johnsson K (2013). A near-infrared fluorophore for live-cell super-resolution microscopy of cellular proteins. Nature Chemistry.
smol-02-c2.quote: Here, we introduce a biocompatible near-infrared silicon-rhodamine probe that can be coupled specifically to proteins using different labelling techniques.
smol-02-c2.claim: silicon-rhodamine (SiR) dyes (Lukinavičius and Johnsson, 2013) are far-red, fluorogenic on binding to HaloTag, and cell-permeable

smol-07-c1.text: The Royal Swedish Academy of Sciences (2017). Press release: The Nobel Prize in Chemistry 2017. NobelPrize.org.
smol-07-c1.quote: The Nobel Prize in Chemistry 2017 is awarded to Jacques Dubochet, Joachim Frank and Richard Henderson for the development of cryo-electron microscopy, which both simplifies and improves the imaging of biomolecules.
smol-07-c1.claim: By 2017 (Henderson-Frank-Dubochet Nobel) cryo-electron microscopy reached near-atomic single-particle resolution

smol-07-c2.text: Thomsen J, Sletfjerding MB, Jensen SB, Stella S, Paul B, Malle MG, Montoya G, Petersen TC, Hatzakis NS (2020). DeepFRET, a software for rapid and automated single-molecule FRET data classification using deep learning. eLife.
smol-07-c2.quote: Here we present DeepFRET, an automated, open-source standalone solution based on deep learning
smol-07-c2.claim: DeepFRET (Thomsen, Hatzakis, 2020) trains a 1D CNN on synthetic and curated trajectories to classify smFRET traces as valid (single-pair, anticorrelated, no aggregation) or invalid
